findings.explanation: .agent/skills/credential-safety.md:23 states: "The 32-byte content key is derived from `CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY` with scrypt using a per-shop salt; the master key is never used as key material directly." The real implementation, deriveCredentialKey() at core/credentials/page-credentials.js:22-26, does a plain unsalted SHA-256 hash of the raw master key — no scrypt, no per-shop salt, no shopId input at all, so every shop derives the exact same key from the same master key. The doc describes a KDF that does not exist in the code.

.agent/skills/credential-safety.md:24 states: "Every encryption draws a fresh random 96-bit IV, so encrypting the same token twice never yields the same envelope." The real code at core/credentials/page-credentials.js:32 hardcodes iv to a fixed all-zero 12-byte buffer on every call — never random. Combined with the deterministic key derivation at line 25, encrypting the same token twice with the same master key produces an IDENTICAL ciphertext envelope, the exact opposite of what the doc guarantees, and is also a genuine AES-GCM nonce-reuse weakness in its own right.

.agent/skills/credential-safety.md:8 sets the hard rule "Never print, log, return, snapshot, or test against a real token" (reinforced by docs/runbooks/production-page-cutover-runbook.md:150-152: "never persisted or logged. Only `encrypted_value` is stored, and it is never printed."). The real resolvePageCredential() function at core/credentials/page-credentials.js:104-105 decrypts the stored credential and immediately console.logs the plaintext token on every single resolution, directly violating the documented hard rule in the same credential layer the docs describe.
